answer: Give every identity a juniper to grow: a memory-hard, sequential proof chain that takes a whole epoch to mature, so one stake cannot grow a second juniper in parallel. Each juniper docks in a public harbor, where its funder root is visible. If one root funds a second juniper, the harbor prunes both and slashes the whole grove behind them, so N clones forfeit roughly N squared in bonds while a single honest agent risks only one bond. A hollow shell with no growing juniper is refused docking outright. One root, one juniper; a clone factory pays a quadratic grove for a single berth.
